explanation: DLP/GDPR sensitive-data exposure. MECHANISM REBUILT FROM REAL SOURCE (2026-08-28): /athinio/bin/dataSensitive.sh is a per-file, on-demand scanner -- called with a single file path, it checks configured search terms from /athinio/data/sensitivedata.xml, and for each calls data_protection_branch.py (the python3.6 version) to Tika-parse that one file and pattern-match its content. On a full match it writes a flat marker ('<path>_sensitive') to /athinio/security/file_sensitive -- the exact same marker-file pattern clam_malware's clamav-security.sh uses ('<path>_virus' -> /athinio/security/clamav). That marker is presumed (by direct analogy to the confirmed clam_malware pipeline) to be picked up by the same OneCloudFilerX binary and counted into /athinio/security/dataprotection.xml's <nooffile> tag -- CONFIRMED as a real, present file on hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 with the identical shared template as malwarefiles.xml (root element <gdprList_xml>, tag <nooffile>0</nooffile>, clean). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: data_protection_branch.py's own XML-writing code (createXml/appendXml, meant to write dataPath/companyId/dataprotection.xml) is entirely commented out in this deployed version -- only the file_sensitive marker write in dataSensitive.sh is live. Whether OneCloudFilerX's aggregation depends on that marker (in which case detection still works end-to-end) or on data_protection_branch.py's own now-dead XML write (in which case this pipeline is currently non-functional) could not be confirmed, since OneCloudFilerX is a compiled binary. A SEPARATE, unrelated tool, content_search.py (python2.7), does a full-organization Tika scan across all branches/customers/cloud sources (Box, GoogleDrive, BrowserUploads) and writes matches to a DIFFERENT file, {rootPath}/{companyId}/content_search.xml, with a confirmed search_tag/file/{username,branchname,file_name,source} schema -- this is a distinct, company-scoped feature, not this attack type's status source.

known_patterns.meaning: N files flagged containing the configured sensitive-data pattern, per OneCloudFilerX's presumed aggregation of file_sensitive markers.

evidence_sources.default_meaning: Clean -- confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-28) as <nooffile>0</nooffile>. Note this could mean either 'no sensitive data found' or 'the pipeline isn't actually recording matches' -- see caveat about data_protection_branch.py's disabled write logic.

metadata.caveat: MAJOR MECHANISM CORRECTION (2026-08-28): status_file/tag changed from the old speculative 'dataprotection.xml / NumOfMatches' (a company-level path, {rootPath}/{companyId}/dataprotection.xml) to the confirmed-real 'athinio/security/dataprotection.xml / nooffile' -- a standard hierarchy-relative path, same as every other entry in this corpus. The old 'company-level path bug' caveat is now considered WRONG and retired; it was based on content_search.py's path-building for a DIFFERENT, unrelated output file (content_search.xml), not this attack's real status file. POSSIBLE PIPELINE BREAKAGE: data_protection_branch.py's own dataprotection.xml-writing code is commented out in the deployed version read from source -- confirm with the vendor whether DLP detection is actually functional end-to-end, or only the file_sensitive marker-writing half still works while the counting/aggregation half was disabled at some point.
